Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: Absolutive is consistently unmarked (zero) for both nouns and pronouns. Ergative is overtly marked with nasal-bearing allomorphs (-n, -an, -man, -nin).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comment: 1st person singular (ena/eah/ea) and 1st person plural exclusive (enabo/eahbo/eabo) show TRIPARTITE alignment: A≠S≠P. Not ergative.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comment: 2nd person singular (mi/mi/mia) and plural (mibo/mibo/miabo) show ACCUSATIVE alignment: A=S≠P. Not ergative. Variation toward tripartite and ergative also attested (Table 31, Table 32).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comment: 3rd person singular (oaton/oa/oa) and plural (aboton/abo/abo) show ERGATIVE alignment: A≠S=P. 1st person plural inclusive (non(bo)/no(bo)/no(bo)) also ergative.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comment: Full nouns systematically show ergative alignment: A is marked with nasal allomorphs (-n, -an, -man, -nin depending on syllable structure); S and P are unmarked (absolutive = zero). Variation toward neutral (unmarked A) also attested due to language obsolescence.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comment: No aspect-conditioned split is described. Ergative marking on full NPs applies in both imperfective (-i) and perfective (-a) contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comment: No aspect-conditioned split is described. Ergative marking on full NPs applies in both perfective (-a) and imperfective (-i) contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comment: No tense-conditioned split is described. Iskonawa has a graded tense system (remote past, recent past, etc.) but none of these conditions ergative marking.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comment: No tense-conditioned split is described. Ergative marking on full NPs applies in non-past contexts as well.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comment: No mood-conditioned split is described for full NPs. Ergative marking applies in indicative contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comment: Desiderative and immediate purpose constructions of transitive verbs take an S-type (absolutive) subject instead of an A-type (ergative) subject — a double-absolutive construction. This constitutes a split in the ergative pattern conditioned by irrealis/modal contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comment: No realis/irrealis split is explicitly described for full NPs in realis contexts. Ergative marking applies.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comment: Desiderative constructions (irrealis) may double-absolutive pattern: transitive subject appears in absolutive (S-type) form rather than ergative. This is a neutralization of ergative marking in irrealis/modal contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comment: No agentivity-conditioned split is described. Ergative marking on full NPs applies regardless of agentivity of A.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: No topicality-conditioned split is described for full NPs.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comment: No animacy-conditioned split is described for full NPs. Ergative marking applies to animate and inanimate A arguments alike.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: Ergative marking on full NPs is documented primarily in main clauses throughout the grammar.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in complement clauses?
Comment: Nominalization is the main strategy for complement clauses. The internal syntax of nominalized clauses is not fully described with respect to case marking. Uncertain.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in adverbial clauses?
Comment: Switch-reference suffixes (-hon for S/A>A, -ah for S/A>S) operate on {A,S} vs. {P}, consistent with ergative alignment in adverbial/chained clauses.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in relative clauses?
Comment: Relative clauses are formed via nominalization. Case marking inside nominalized relative clauses is not explicitly described. Uncertain.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in other non-main clauses?
Comment: Insufficient data in the grammar to determine case marking in all non-main clause types. Uncertain.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by other factors?
Comment: OBSOLESCENCE: free variation between ergative and neutral (unmarked A) in 3rd person and full NPs.

Feature: Is the ergative marker the same as the genitive marker?
Comment: The dominant ergative allomorph -nin is formally identical to the genitive suffix -nin (§6.4.1). E.g., German-nin (ERG) 'Germán-ERG' vs. German-nin (GEN) 'Germán's'. The other ergative allomorphs (-n, -an, -man) are distinct from the genitive.

Feature: Is the ergative marker the same as the instrumental/comitative marker?
Comment: Instrumental is -pan (§6.3.2), distinct from all ergative allomorphs (-n, -an, -man, -nin). Comitative is -be(tan) (§6.3.4), also distinct. No syncretism between ergative and instrumental/comitative.
